commands.name: get-product
commands.summary: Get a food product's name, common name and Nutri-Score breakdown by barcode (EAN/UPC), parsed from its product page

commands.name: get-product-questions
commands.summary: List the Robotoff machine-generated questions (for example a suggested category or label to confirm) that are pending for a product barcode

commands.name: list-countries
commands.summary: List the countries Open Food Facts supports, as a map from country code (e.g. us, fr) to English country name

commands.name: list-attribute-groups
commands.summary: List the product attribute groups used for personalized ranking (nutritional quality, processing, allergens, environment, …) with their attributes and allowed values

commands.name: list-preference-levels
commands.summary: List the importance levels a user can assign to a product attribute (not important, important, very important, mandatory) with their scoring factors

commands.name: list-external-sources
commands.summary: List the external knowledge-panel providers (for example the animal-welfare Suffering Footprint) and the product filters each one applies to

commands.name: list-data-exports
commands.summary: List the nightly database dump and export downloads (MongoDB dump, CSV, JSONL, …) with their download and checksum links

dropped.name: get-product-folksonomy
dropped.reason: The endpoint itself works: HTTP 200 with a JSON array. But the example barcode 3017620422003 has no folksonomy tags, so the response is an empty list ([]). I couldn't find a barcode in the recording or live evidence that returns tags. Swapping in an unverified example would just be a guess. Re-add this command once an example barcode with folksonomy tags can be confirmed.
